triangle-sections-solid.alt: A 3D view of a solid on the region under y = √x from x = 0 to 4, lying flat on the floor. Equilateral triangles stand on the base, each perpendicular to the x-axis with one side across the base, so the triangle at x has side s = √x; one is highlighted in blue. A side panel shows the triangle with side s and height (√3/2)s, its area (√3/4)s², and the volume, the integral from 0 to 4 of (√3/4)(√x)² dx = 2√3, compared with 8 for squares on the same base.

semicircle-sections-solid.alt: A 3D view of the same base, the region under y = √x from x = 0 to 4, with semicircles standing on it, each perpendicular to the x-axis with its diameter across the base, so the diameter at x is s = √x; one is highlighted in green. A side panel shows the semicircle with diameter s and radius s/2, its area (π/8)s², and the volume, the integral from 0 to 4 of (π/8)(√x)² dx = π. Using s as the radius would make the answer 4 times too big.
